title: Psalm 1:1–2 — blessing is not mere abstinence, but will in the law
english: “Blessed is the man who has not walked in the counsel of the ungodly, and has not stood in the way of sinners, and has not sat on the seat of pestilent ones. But his will is in the law of the Lord, and in his law he will meditate day and night” (Psalm 1:1-2).

Blessed, then, is the one who longs for the things that truly are. But how is the blessing in a taking-away of evils? For abstinence from evils is common also to the soulless and to the irrational. For this reason, then, he added: “But his will is in the law of the Lord.” For this belongs not only to a rational being, but is also the beginning of taking up the good things: the flight from evils. “Turn from evil,” he says, “and do good” (Psalm 34:14). For as on a ladder the first ascent is withdrawal from the earth, so in the progress according to God, the separation from evil.

But also in general every idleness is easier than even a chance action: such as “You shall not commit adultery, you shall not fornicate” (Exodus 20:14) and the rest, which need each person’s idleness and not-moving. But “You shall love your neighbor” (Leviticus 19:18; Matthew 22:39), and “Sell your belongings and give to the poor” (Matthew 19:21), and “If anyone conscripts you one mile, go with him two” (Matthew 5:41) are already deeds of a youthful soul and of athletes.

If he had set the perfect things before you at once, you would have shrunk from the undertaking; but now he trains you beforehand with the more easily grasped, so that you may dare the things next. As deeds fitting for athletes, we already need a youthful soul toward the achievement; so wonder at the wisdom of the one who leads us through the easier and more easily grasped toward perfection.

The “way of sinners” can be said to be the devil; the one who has come to be in it must not remain, according to “Resist the devil, and he will flee from you” (James 4:7). For the one who has not stood in it will come to the Lord, who said “I am the way” (John 14:6); coming to be in it and running according to the mark, he will obtain the prizes. “Ungodly”: those who do not know God. “On a seat”: the working of evils, come about by succession. “But in the law”: the evangelical, clearly. “He will meditate”: by his counsel.
translator_notes: Tip of Origen Fragmenta in Psalmos (Greek), PG 12 / Khazarzar. Psalm 1:1–2. Scaffold Unit-1 English discarded, not globbed. OCR spacing restored where the word is clear. No modern English copied.

title: Psalm 1:3 — the tree is Christ, transplanted, beside the scriptures
english: “And he will be as the tree planted beside the outlets of the waters, which will give its fruit in its season, and its leaf will not fall away, and everything he may do will prosper” (Psalm 1:3).

A tree, Christ is written in the God-breathed Scripture. Aquila rendered “transplanted”: for rooted in the patriarchs’ roots, he is transplanted so that others also may partake of his image, taken according to the being-transplanted; or it is said of the Savior’s soul transplanted from here into paradise. For he said to the robber: “Today you will be with me in the paradise of God” (Luke 23:43). “Outlets of waters”: the divine scriptures, in which everywhere one can find Christ proclaimed.

The fruit of the tree you will understand as the right faith. Its leaves, the fulfillment of the commandments. And one of the saints used to say that leaves are the ascetics’ humility, covering their fruits and never falling. “It will prosper”: for there is no deed of those done according to God that is useless.
translator_notes: Psalm 1:3. Aquila μεταπεφυτευμένον kept as transplanted. Paradise word to the robber is Luke 23:43 as printed. Scaffold discarded.

title: Psalm 1:4–6 — the ungodly do not rise into judgment; the way perishes, not the substances
english: “Not so the ungodly, not so” (Psalm 1:4). Some prefix a second “not so”; but neither did the Hebrew double the word, nor did any of those who translated use a repetition of the phrase.
“Therefore the ungodly will not rise in judgment” (Psalm 1:5). Having said the ungodly will not rise, he says “into judgment,” not “into questioning.”

“Because the Lord knows the way of the righteous, and the way of the ungodly will perish” (Psalm 1:6). “Knows” instead of “honors,” according to what was said by God to Moses: “I know you above all, and you have found favor with me” (Exodus 33:17). It is to be noted universally that only the good is known by the Lord; for the way of the righteous is good; but also “the Lord knew those who are his” (2 Timothy 2:19) and the way of the righteous, having said “I am the way” (John 14:6).

The way of the ungodly is the one walked by those who speak evil of the Creator, becoming like chaff thrown from the wind; therefore they are not counted worthy of the resurrection in judgment, as neither are sinners of the counsel of the righteous. For the way of the righteous, being worthy of God’s knowledge, is known by him; but the way of the ungodly will perish, as not being known by the Lord.

And having said that the way of the ungodly perishes, he corrected the suspicions of the heretics who supposed their substances are made to vanish into non-being, from what was said: “but as the chaff which the wind throws from the face of the earth” (Psalm 1:4). For when the way has perished, the ungodliness becomes non-existent, those to whom it happened being left.
translator_notes: Psalm 1:4–6. Some witnesses double οὐχ οὕτως; lock notes Hebrew and the translators do not. γινώσκει = honors, with Exodus 33:17. Heretics who annihilate substances are corrected: the way perishes, the persons remain. Scaffold discarded.

title: Psalm 2 hypothesis — the first psalm is almost the title of the second
english: Hypothesis. But since not to be ungodly was set first in the beginning of the blessing, the second word sets out the things that have come to be outside ungodliness, the evangelical mystery spoken beforehand; so that in a way the first psalm is an inscription of the second.

For it speaks the generation through flesh there of Christ who has been begotten “today” for us (and “today” is a part of time), but who always is Son and God from the Father and in the Father; and it speaks the kingdom over those without a king, who because they did not slave for God had been counted among the nations.
translator_notes: Psalm 2 hypothesis (2.π). First psalm as inscription of the second. σήμερον kept as today, a part of time. Lock brackets [τὰ] [λέγει] unrestored as printed. Scaffold not globbed.

title: Psalm 2:3–5 — burst their bonds; he who dwells in the heavens will laugh
english: “Let us burst their bonds, and throw off their yoke from us” (Psalm 2:3). For the nations are squeezed by their own sins, not being free; therefore Christ says this, either to the angels who serve him, or to the Father and the Holy Spirit, or to the apostles the servants of the gospel, calling on them to tear their bonds apart.

The peoples, being bodily under the yoke of the law — which contains ordinances that are not good and commandments that are not good — when they are brought through Christ to the spiritual law, which has the good ordinances and commandments, put off the heavy yoke of the letter that kills, the Savior saying to the fellow-workers already named: “Let us throw off their yoke from us,” that is, let us make this from ourselves, not waiting for the request of those who are burdened. Or as he himself also came under the law (for it was written: and he was circumcised, and he followed their sabbaths), that is, from me and from those who are persuaded, or at least counting their yoke our burden because of love toward them, let us throw it off. These things, then, about men, both from the nations and from the people.

“He who dwells in the heavens will laugh at them, and the Lord will mock them” (Psalm 2:4). “He who dwells in the heavens will laugh at them” is toward the kings of the earth, whom the Lord in the heavens will laugh at, as having an earthly mind and not having understood the wisdom about the Savior’s becoming-man. And he will mock the rulers also. And it was fitting for the Son of God to say: even if the nations have cried out and the peoples have meditated empty things, we will burst the bonds of the one and throw off the yoke of the other, since they no longer receive the healing easily. For they did not want to come inside the holy net, about which it is written: “The kingdom of the heavens is like a net thrown into the sea” (Matthew 13:47).

“Then he will speak to them in his anger” (Psalm 2:5). Anger of God is a toilsome chastisement for the benefit of the one who has sinned. But also in the time of the judgment they will taste the anger of God, and all the enemies of the saving Word will be troubled by his wrath. He did not say “he will chastise them,” but “he will speak to them in his anger”; for when they repent he did not chastise, as with the Ninevites. For God threatens toward salvation, he said, and to the Ninevites he sent Jonah.
translator_notes: Psalm 2:3–5. Yoke of the letter that kills vs spiritual law. Circumcision and sabbaths of the Savior as printed. Net = Matthew 13:47. Anger speaks, does not necessarily chastise (Nineveh / Jonah). Scaffold not globbed.

title: Psalm 2:7–12 — today I have begotten you; take hold of training
english: “I have begotten you today” (Psalm 2:7). “Today” is always being called.
“Ask of me, and I will give you nations, your inheritance” (Psalm 2:8). The devil showed the Savior their kingdoms and the glory in a moment of time.

“Take hold of training” (Psalm 2:12). Training is a measured-suffering of the passions, which is naturally apt to come about from the practical life; and the practical life is a spiritual teaching, cleansing the passionate part of the soul.
translator_notes: Psalm 2:7–12 as the lock has them (2.7, 2.8, 2.12; no 2.9–2.11 in this block). σήμερον always being called. Devil's showing of kingdoms is the gospel temptation as printed. παιδεία = training / measured-suffering of passions. Scaffold not globbed.

title: Psalm 3:2–4 — those who progress have many afflicters; the Lord lifts the head
english: “Lord, why have those who afflict me been multiplied?” (Psalm 3:2). Those who are making progress have many who afflict them.

“But you, Lord, are my helper, my glory, and the one who lifts up my head” (Psalm 3:4). Then the mind is lifted up, whenever it applies itself to the manifold wisdom of God (Ephesians 3:10). The glory of the holy one is God. And everyone whose glory is God is lifted up by him.

The head, that is, the rising of the soul. For just as the head of one who has been made large in body is lifted up above the heads of the lesser ones that lie below, so also, when the soul of the blessed has risen, the head is lifted up, God working with it.
translator_notes: Psalm 3:2 and 3.4 from locked PG 12. CF crib inverted προκόπτοντες, ἐπιβάλλῃ, πολυποικίλῳ, and ἔπαρμα; not globbed. OCR spacing restored where the word is clear. πολυποικίλῳ σοφίᾳ as printed (Ephesians 3:10). ἀντιλήπτωρ = helper. ἔπαρμα = rising/exaltation, not perfection. Scaffold not globbed.

title: Psalm 3:5 — the holy mountain may be the Only-begotten
english: “And he heard me from his holy mountain” (Psalm 3:5). See whether the holy mountain can be the Only-begotten, from where God will hear.
translator_notes: Psalm 3:5. ὄρος ἅγιον, not mouth. Μονογενής kept as Only-begotten. CF crib read ὄρους as mouth and made the Only-begotten a voice; not globbed.

title: Psalm 3:8 — he arises for some and strikes those hostile in vain
english: “Arise, Lord, save me, my God, because you have struck all who are hostile to me in vain. You have crushed the teeth of sinners” (Psalm 3:8). To each, God has a certain state: those for whom he has arisen, those he also saves; but those who are hostile in vain he strikes.

And of those hostile in vain, such is also this: “they hated me without a cause” (John 15:25). And of what sort are the teeth of sinners crushed by the Lord, such also are these about whom it is said: “there will be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth” (Matthew 8:12); and “the teeth of the one who has eaten the unripe grape will be set on edge” (Jeremiah 31:29).
translator_notes: Psalm 3:8. ματαίως = in vain, distinct from δωρεάν = without a cause. Teeth of sinners crushed by the Lord, not the Lord's teeth. ὄμφαξ = unripe grape; αἱμωδιᾶν = teeth set on edge, not blood. CF crib inverted both and truncated; not globbed. Lock has no 3.1, 3.3, 3.6, 3.7 in this block.

title: Psalm 4 inscription — Unto the end; the end is to be made alive in Christ
english: “Unto the end, in psalms, a song to David.” Hypothesis. Many psalms having, according to the Seventy, the inscription “Unto the end,” but according to the rest the things corresponding to “Unto the end” that are here rendered, it is worthwhile, as far as power allows, to track out the sense indicated by the wording.

It is to be known that, just as of every art and science there is an end, toward which the one who genuinely pursues the art or the science hastens, so also of the rational nature there must be an end. And this is to be made alive in Christ, according to the things said by Paul the most wise in the first letter to the Corinthians: “For as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all will be made alive, but each in his own order” (1 Corinthians 15:22-23).

But as far as saying “in his own order,” he does not sketch one end of all; for it is likely that each will be made alive according to the worth of the things done, either coming to this without torment, or after punishments.
And Christ, having made alive in himself all who die in Adam, reigns over those who have been made alive.
We think, then, that the psalms inscribed “Unto the end” inscribe some sense of the end, and summon those who understand the things said toward that.

And for everyone who contends, the victory also happens to be the end. Many, then, are the victories according to part, and an end, as of Paul when he says: “In all these things we more than conquer through him who loved us” (Romans 8:37), and when: “I have fought the good fight, I have finished the course, I have kept the faith; henceforth there is laid up for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will give me on that day, and not only to me but to all who have loved his appearing” (2 Timothy 4:7-8).
translator_notes: Psalm 4.1 inscription and hypothesis from locked PG 12. CF crib score-ok but Οʹ=ninth, ἄξιον ὅσῃ δύναμις as vocative, λογικῆς=logical, οὐχ ἓν τέλος as 'not the end for all', βάσανος=trial, ὑπερνικῶμεν=overcome, Pass A a summary; not globbed. OCR spacing restored where the word is clear. τέλος kept as end, not choirmaster. λοιπούς = the rest of the translators. Scaffold not globbed.

title: Psalm 4:2 — he heard me in the calling, and in affliction you widened me
english: “In my calling, the God of my righteousness heard me; in affliction you widened me” (Psalm 4:2).
He did not hear me after the calling, but in the calling. When we come to know the reasons of the afflictions and of the trials, then especially we are widened.

Even if as a man the prophet calls, and because of the calling is heard by the God of his righteousness — I mean the righteousness of the one speaking — and for this reason comes to be in a widening in the times of affliction, still, as toward God, being such, he is below. For the eyes of the Lord are high, and man is low, and he needs to be pitied by God.
translator_notes: Psalm 4:2. ἐν τῷ ἐπικαλεῖσθαι = in the calling, not after. πλατύνω = widen. CF crib not globbed. Scaffold not globbed.

title: Psalm 4:3 — sons of men, how long heavy-hearted; evil is a heavy nature
english: “Sons of men, how long heavy-hearted?” (Psalm 4:3). “Sons of men,” someone will suppose, has been said by periphrasis, as it is also the custom of Greeks to use such a figure, saying “sons of the Achaeans” and the like.
Here we know that evil is of a heavy nature; therefore the Lord, coming into Egypt, is said to sit upon a light cloud. And a light cloud is a rational nature, filled with every virtue and knowledge.
translator_notes: Psalm 4:3. υἱοὶ ἀνθρώπων may be periphrasis like υἱεῖς Ἀχαιῶν. Evil is heavy; the Lord on a light cloud into Egypt. Scaffold not globbed.

title: Psalm 4:4 — know that the Lord has made his holy one wonderful; believing is not the same as knowing
english: “And know that the Lord has made his holy one wonderful” (Psalm 4:4).

Know, then, you who have trusted in multitudes, that he has shown as wonderful the one who has trusted in him. David prophesies about Christ in the fifteenth psalm, that he is a true holy one, and the apostles are witnesses about him, having understood: “nor will you give your holy one to see corruption” (Psalm 16:10).

And it is possible also to be taught about every holy one. But to believe and to know are not the same; as neither is it the same to believe the truth and to know the truth, and to believe God and to know God. Therefore to the apostles already having believed the Savior says: “If you remain in my word, you are truly my disciples, and you will know the truth, and the truth will free you” (John 8:31-32). For as Isaiah says: “If you do not believe, you will not understand” (Isaiah 7:9). And David: “I believed, therefore I spoke” (Psalm 116:10). And “Be still and know that I am God” (Psalm 46:10) makes clear that knowing differs from believing; for this was not said to the unbelieving.

And it also shows what sort of knowledge it will be necessary to receive, and how the holy ones have been made wonderful by God, having been led to the wonders of the unspeakable mysteries and of the holy contemplations.
translator_notes: Psalm 4:4. Fifteenth psalm / “your holy one to see corruption” is Psalm 16:10 (LXX 15). Believing ≠ knowing (John 8:31-32; Isaiah 7:9; Psalm 116:10; Psalm 46:10). Dropped printed page-mark Μεγάλη ββ. p. 560 from the reading English. Scaffold not globbed.

title: Psalm 4:5 — be angry and do not sin; do not confirm anger by the deed
english: “Be angry, and do not sin” (Psalm 4:5).
He exhorts not to assent to the appearance, nor to bring on the deed confirming the anger.
translator_notes: Psalm 4.5 from locked PG 12. CF crib score-ok but κυροῦν=rule (κυριεύω), φαντασία=phantasy, ἔργον ἐπάγειν inverted, Pass A a summary that imported stray Θυσία as this verse’s point; not globbed. Θυσία sits between τὴν and ὀργήν in the lock; it is the next lemma (4.6 θυσίαν), not part of this comment. OCR spacing restored (φαντασίᾳ, ἔργον). Scaffold not globbed.

title: Psalm 4:6 — sacrifice a sacrifice of righteousness; hope is expectation of true knowledge
english: “Sacrifice a sacrifice of righteousness, and hope upon the Lord” (Psalm 4:6).
Righteousness is impassibility of a rational soul, offered to God; and hope is a good expectation of true knowledge.
translator_notes: Psalm 4:6. δικαιοσύνη = impassibility of a rational soul offered to God. ἐλπίς = good expectation of true knowledge. Scaffold not globbed.

title: Psalm 4:7 — the light of your face; angels see the face, men the light
english: “The light of your face has been marked upon us, Lord” (Psalm 4:7).

The angels always see the face of God; but men, the light of his face. For the face of the Lord is a spiritual contemplation of all things that have come to be on earth. And the light of the face is the partial knowledge of these same things, if according to the wise Tekoite: “David was as an angel of God, knowing all things on the earth” (2 Samuel 14:17).
translator_notes: Psalm 4:7. Angels see the face; men the light of the face. Θηκωΐτις = the Tekoite woman (2 Samuel 14). μερική γνῶσις = partial knowledge. Scaffold not globbed.

title: Psalm 4:8 — gladness from wheat, wine, and oil; intelligible, not sensible
english: “You gave gladness into my heart, from fruit of wheat and wine and oil” (Psalm 4:8).

These things are promised in many places of the Scripture to the holy, and the deprivation of them is threatened to sinners — clearly of the intelligible and not of the sensible. Some, thinking them evils because of the smallness of the promise, wanted to worship another God fabricated by them. For when it partakes of the better things, each soul is both sanctified and in good condition toward being able to complete the works that fall to it.

And into the coming age Paul also brought these: “Let no one judge you in food or in drink, or in part of a feast, or new moon, sabbaths, which are a shadow of the things to come” (Colossians 2:16-17). Wheat and wine and oil multiply sinners; but the gladness of God gladdens the righteous.
translator_notes: Psalm 4:8. Wheat, wine, oil are intelligible, not sensible. Other-god worship from thinking the promise small. Colossians 2:16-17 as printed. Scaffold not globbed.

title: Psalm 5 inscription — Unto the end, concerning the inheriting one; Christ’s inheritance is the rational nature
english: “Unto the end, concerning the inheriting one” (Psalm 5 inscription).
The inheritance of Christ is the rational nature.
translator_notes: Psalm 5.1 from locked PG 12. CF crib score-ok but κληρονομούσης=inheritance (κληρονομίας), lemma mixed with the comment, Pass A a summary that invented a missing sigma; not globbed. κληρονομούσης is the feminine participle (her who inherits), the LXX title; Origen’s comment then names Christ’s inheritance as the rational nature. λογική=rational, not logical. Scaffold not globbed.

title: Psalm 5:8 — I will worship toward your holy temple in your fear; the temple is Christ
english: “I will worship toward your holy temple in your fear” (Psalm 5:8).

A holy temple of God is Christ, because “God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself” (2 Corinthians 5:19). In the fear of God everyone turns aside from evil (Proverbs 16:6); and in the fear of the Lord he worships the temple, which is Christ: for “Destroy this temple,” he says, “and in three days I will raise it” (John 2:19).
translator_notes: Psalm 5.8 from locked PG 12. NV crib score-ok but read OCR ναὸν α γιόν as temple of the Son (ἅγιόν), λύσατε=loose, φησίν=they say, and pasted a citation tag onto every sentence; not globbed. ἅγιόν restored as holy. Ναὸς ἅγιός ἐστι τοῦ Θεοῦ ὁ Χριστός = a holy temple of God is Christ, not the Son of God as the temple. λύσατε in John 2:19 is Destroy. Scaffold not globbed.

title: Psalm 5:9 — lead me in your righteousness because of my enemies; they are intelligible
english: “Lord, lead me in your righteousness, because of my enemies” (Psalm 5:9).

In the righteousness according to practice, in Christ. — “Of my enemies.” The intelligible ones, clearly; for many are those who plot against the God-loving soul, begrudging its progress according to God.
translator_notes: Psalm 5.9 from locked PG 12. CF crib usable but A==B score-fail: προκοπῇ=cutting (κόπος), διαβασκαίνοντες=passing through (διαβαίνω), νοητῶν=things, δηλονότι split as δη, ἕνεκα as ἐν ἐκα; not globbed. προκοπή=progress; διαβασκαίνω=begrudge; νοητῶν agrees with ἐχθρῶν. OCR ἕνεκα / δηλονότι / προκοπῇ restored. Scaffold not globbed.

title: Psalm 5:10 — no truth in their mouth; their throat an opened tomb filled with dead works
english: “Because there is no truth in their mouth; their heart is vain” (Psalm 5:10). First, there is no truth except Christ; and perhaps the second clause has borne their plot.
“An opened tomb is their throat” (Psalm 5:10). Filled with dead works.
translator_notes: Psalm 5.10 from locked PG 12. CF crib usable but A==B score-fail: Πρότερον=previously, ἤ dropped so ‘the Christ’ not exceptive, Τάφος lemma glued into the first comment, ἠνέγκατο=caused, ἐπιβουλήν=according to counsel, νεκρῶν ἔργων=works of the dead; not globbed. ἤ after οὐδεμία = except. ἠνέγκατο (φέρω middle) = bore. OCR put the second lemma between καὶ τάχα τὸ and δεύτερον; restored as two lemma-comment pairs. Scaffold not globbed.
